encounters.cc: Sudden episode of difficulty breathing and cyanosis while crying.

lines: Sudden episode of difficulty breathing and cyanosis while crying.
The patient is an infant with known Tetralogy of Fallot, severe combined immunodeficiency, and Down syndrome who presents to the emergency department with acute cyanosis and difficulty breathing.
He has received recent outpatient care for congenital cytomegalovirus infection, congenital toxoplasmosis, and failure to thrive.
The parents report that these episodes have been occurring more frequently over the past month.
- Severe combined immunodeficiency (MHC Class II deficiency/Bare Lymphocyte Syndrome)
- Pompe disease (Glycogen Storage Disease Type II)
The child was diagnosed with tetralogy of Fallot shortly after birth.
- Palliative or complete repair of Tetralogy of Fallot
- Ferrous sulfate 3 mg/kg/day of elemental iron
- Alglucosidase alfa 20 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks (enzyme replacement)
- Calcium carbonate 75 mg/kg/day divided TID (hypocalcemia prophylaxis)
- Advanced maternal age at conception (mother >35 years)
- Maternal history of primary infection with Toxoplasma gondii and CMV during pregnancy
- One deceased sibling in infancy with similar presentation (possible genetic condition)
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Pediatric patient.
Oxygen saturation of 76% on room air.
His heart rate is 160 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 60 breaths per minute, and blood pressure is 80/50 mmHg.
On examination, the infant is irritable, tachypneic, and cyanotic.
A harsh systolic murmur is audible at the left upper sternal border.
The child's extremities are cool to the touch, and capillary refill time is 4 seconds.
The rest of the physical examination is unremarkable.
The parents are instructed to place the child in a knee-chest position, and supplemental oxygen is provided.
